paper_title: Knowing You Don't Know Learning When to Continue Search in Multi-round   RAG through Self-Practicing
caption: Ablation study on different Inner Monologue turns on HotPotQA. The green line represents the Naive Generation baseline, while the blue line shows the performance of SIM-RAGlite. The red line indicates the EM score using the ground-truth label as an Oracle Critic.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the effect of varying the number of inner monologue turns on the Exact Match (EM) performance of different RAG systems on the HotPotQA dataset. The x-axis, labeled "Turns of Inner Monologue," ranges from 0 to 6 in integer increments, representing the number of iterative reasoning steps. The y-axis, labeled "EM (%)", measures the performance in percentage, ranging from 0 to 50 with major gridlines at intervals of 10. The plot compares three methods: "Naive Gen" (green line with 'x' markers), "SIM-RAG (lite)" (blue line with 'x' markers), and "SIM-RAG (Oracle Critic)" (red line with 'x' markers). The green line remains flat at an EM score of 20% across all 7 turns, indicating no improvement with additional reasoning. The blue line shows a steady increase from approximately 15.5% at 0 turns to about 30% at 6 turns. The red line demonstrates the highest performance, starting at 20% and rising sharply to approximately 47% at 6 turns, indicating the benefit of using an oracle critic to guide the search process.
